# 📋 OPEN-ITEMS — the single registry (W0)

**The one place deferred/open work lives.** Created by W0 (PRODUCTION_PLAN §W0) because closure state
was scattered across four docs with drift — which is exactly how "all boxes checked" and "not
production-ready" were both true. **Updating this file is part of the "Gate before done" checklist**
(CLAUDE.md): when your change closes, opens, or retires an item, sweep it here in the same PR.

Severity: **blocker** (ship-stopper on its surface) · **high** (real security/money/ops gap) ·
**med** (correctness/a11y with a plausible trigger) · **low** (hardening/polish) · **config** (needs
Min, not code). Status: **open** · **planned:Wx** (owned by a W-track phase) · **gated** (external
prerequisite). Closed items move to the Closed section with the closing PR — don't delete rows.

| C16 | **high** | **Make `codex-review` a REQUIRED status check on `main`, or the whole gate protects nothing.** `.github/workflows/require-codex-review.yml` (2026-08-29, owner: _"wire the wait into the flow properly"_) publishes its verdict as a check run named **`codex-review`**, created against the PR head — red until Codex has reviewed the exact commit about to merge, green on its own when it reports. Until branch protection lists that name, it is an advisory red tick that anyone can merge straight past, which is strictly worse than no gate because everyone believes it is working. ⚠️ **Wire `codex-review`, NOT `codex-reviewed`.** The job's implicit check briefly carried the near-identical name `codex-reviewed`, and it is green whenever the gate merely EVALUATES — including when the verdict is red; the job has since been renamed `publish-codex-verdict` so no such lookalike is offered in the settings picker, but a stale `codex-reviewed` entry from before that rename would silently satisfy protection forever. Two consequences worth knowing before turning it on: **(a)** the check is per-HEAD by design, so the last push before a merge always needs one more Codex round — that does not conflict with the two-round budget, which bounds how many rounds are TRIADED, not how many exist; **(b)** drafts publish success deliberately, because an unpublished required check reads as pending and blocks a merge exactly as hard as a red one. **Proven live on #241 (2026-08-29):** marked ready 19:50:52Z, `codex-review` red on the head at 19:51:01Z, squash-merged 19:51:12Z — eleven seconds past the red, by the session that BUILT the gate, and `8f2b11b` (a money-path guard rewrite) reached `main` with no Codex review of it. #242 held only because the merge waited by hand (the ritual is now docs/WORKFLOW.md §Review step 5). This row is no longer hypothetical. | #240 · CLAUDE.md §Codex  |

| M1   | med      | **Q5 — split fulfill reconciles only Σ(shares), never against the cart.** With M25 that makes the guard a tautology. **W10d built a real reconcile and reverted it, and the reason is the durable finding:** a check placed at FULFILLMENT time can only fire after every card is charged (money taken, no order), but moving it BEFORE the capture loop is also wrong as written — `captureAllIfReady` deliberately proceeds on a STALE freeze and is re-entered on the straggler path after a PARTIAL capture, so refusing there does NOT leave the authorizations untouched, and `abortSettlement` then refuses too. Worse, the cart total legitimately MOVES: the webhook burns the applied reward immediately after fulfillment (`mms_reward_discount` filters `redeemed_at is null`) and a time-windowed promo can expire mid-settlement, so every sibling/redelivered `succeeded` event computed a larger expectation and the RPC raised permanently for 72h. The design that works: persist the expected total (and its components) at `openSettlement`, reconcile the ledger against that PINNED value pre-capture, and give a mismatch a durable record + a diner/staff surface rather than a `console.error` and a retry loop. **CLOSED (W11, 2026-08-05)** — `mms_fulfill_split_order` now reconciles Σ(amount − tip) over the captured ledger against `qr_carts.settle_expected_cents`, PINNED at `openSettlement` from the same derivation that produced the shares (a constant, so redeliveries always compute the same verdict — the live-total failure W10d documented cannot recur). The caller-supplied expectation is deleted. A mismatch writes a durable `qr_refunds_needed` row BEFORE raising, and the idempotent branch runs FIRST. An unpinned open fails closed. Migration `20260805210000_w11_split_ledger_durable.sql` is in the repo and CI-verified; **prod `db push` waits for the owner's project restore** — until then prod runs the pre-W11 behaviour. | M70  | med      | **A lapsing promo can push a shrunken basket ABOVE its own authorization, and W23c cancels the whole hold.** `mms_promo_discount` drops a promotion once the subtotal falls under `min_subtotal_cents`, so voiding a sold-out line can RAISE the total: a $30 basket with a $10-off promo requiring $25 authorizes $20; void a $6 line and the $24 subtotal no longer clears the threshold, so the live total is $24 against a $20 hold. `planCapture` returns `over_authorized` and the order is cancelled — SAFE (the guest is never charged a number they did not agree to; capturing $24 is impossible and capturing the $20 hold would bill full price for less food) but poor service, since one small shortage cancels everything. The good answer is to HONOUR an already-authorized promo through settlement, which means teaching the ONE discount authority that a granted promo survives a shortage — a money-path change that deserves its own slice, not an improvisation at the end of W23c. Only bites baskets whose promo sits within the shortage's value of its threshold. **✅ CLOSED (2026-08-25) — and it was FOUR triggers, not one.** `mms_promo_discount` returns 0 on a deleted/deactivated code, `now() < valid_from`, `now() > valid_until`, OR `subtotal < min_subtotal_cents` — and only the last needs a cart change. A hold taken at 23:58 under a promo expiring at midnight cancels at 00:01 with the basket untouched, so the row's "only bites baskets whose promo sits within the shortage's value of its threshold" understated it: wall-clock expiry has no such bound. Owner chose to honour all four. **The grant is PINNED at authorization** (`qr_carts.promo_granted_cents`, written by `mms_pin_promo_grant` BEFORE the amount is derived — ordering is load-bearing, since deriving first would mint an amount from the live value and pin a different one a moment later). The arithmetic is NOT duplicated: the existing body is renamed `mms_promo_discount_live` byte-for-byte and the public reader keeps its signature (zero caller changes) as "pin if present, else live". ⚠️ Also established: the total can only rise when the discount drops to ZERO — `pct` gives S·(1−p) and a partial `flat` gives S−v, both monotone in the subtotal — so those four drops are the whole surface. ⚠️ The pin deliberately OUTLIVES the lock: fulfillment re-derives and reconciles against the captured amount, so clearing at release or capture would raise `reconcile_mismatch`. That inversion is not hypothetical — raising `--surface-elevated` DID put the chrome above the light stop mid-M126, and the audit's `>= 4.5` could never have said so. **What is still open:** `--oa` and `--surface-elevated` are asserted only as CONTRAST pairs, which a wrong-but-legible value still satisfies, and the same PR showed exactly how that bites — light's `--glass-chrome` moved onto a legible-but-forbidden surface and every ratio assertion stayed green. The durable fix is still an identity pin, not another ratio. |
| M128 | low      | ✅ **DONE (2026-08-27, M126) — closed as a side effect, not by tuning the lever it named.** The row's own measurement was right about the culprit (100% of the failing pixels were `--tex-line` grid crossings, 0% were grain) and right that `--tex-grain-opacity` would move nothing. The fix is structural: M126's ambient makes the page grid a **groove** rather than a ridge. A light hairline on a dark ground LIGHTENS the pixel under light text; a dark groove darkens it, so the grid now BUYS contrast instead of spending it. Re-measured with the same compositor across both themes: Night's worst ambient pixel goes **4.4743 → 4.8443** and light's **3.9670 → 4.6428** — and note that the light theme was failing harder than Night and this row never said so, because it only ever looked at Night. `--tex-line` itself is untouched and still lives on `.texture-lines`; what changed is that the page ambient no longer uses it. The bound is now pinned by `composite-contrast.test.ts` rather than by a one-off measurement, so it cannot rot. **The durable lesson stands and is worth re-reading: the contrast audit measures TOKENS, not RENDERED SURFACES** — which is exactly the gap that guard was written to close. | T4   | low | **TS↔SQL tax rounding diverges by 1¢ on NEGATIVE amounts, and negatives are schema-representable.** `tax.ts:37` uses `Math.round` (half toward +∞); `…init.sql:37-38` uses `round(numeric)` (half away from zero). Verified: −200 → TS −19, SQL −20 (also −600/−1000/−1400); `Math.round(-5 * 0.0975)` returns `-0`. The POSITIVE side is exhaustively identical (0…2,000,000 + int4 max, zero disagreements). Representable because `qr_cart_items.unit_price_cents` (`init:156`), `qr_order_items.unit_price_cents` (`:190`) and `modifier_options.price_delta_cents` (`:87`) carry **no `>= 0` CHECK** — unlike `menu_items.base_price_cents` (`:58`) which does. Adding those CHECKs is a migration against live data — its own slice. | T5   | low | ✅ **DONE (2026-08-29) — but only after Codex corrected my first answer, which was WRONG.** This row's harm is "a test placed there is invisible forever with no warning". I first downgraded it, arguing W8's orphan-suite guard already rejected such a file. **Codex P2 on #241 showed that was true only for the `.test` suffix** — the guard enumerated `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx`, so a conventional `packages/db/foo.spec.ts` was neither rejected NOR executed, and the original failure mode survived intact under a different filename. Verified before accepting: `git ls-files -- '*.test.ts'` returns nothing for a `.spec.ts`, and neither vitest config includes `.spec` at any path (`apps/qr` is `**/*.test.ts`, `packages/ui` is `src/**/*.test.ts`). **Fixed** by adding `*.spec.ts` and `*.spec.tsx` to the non-running set beside `*.test.tsx`, in `ci.yml` AND its mirror in `verify-slice.mjs` — a file that can run nowhere is now rejected wherever it sits. Fixing the mirror surfaced a second defect: `find()` took ONE pattern, so the variadic call would have dropped two suffixes into the shell as nothing — a guard quietly looking for less than it claims. It is variadic now. `packages/db` and `packages/config` still define no `test` script, and that stays a design note: they host no tests, and a suite dropped there is now loudly rejected rather than silently skipped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | open        | W8 spec / CI read                             |
| M72b | med | **The app still reads the catalog and still sends `p_menu_ids`, and the function still accepts it — both are deployment-compatibility scaffolding, to be removed together ONCE the migration is live.** M72a deliberately changed no TypeScript. The first draft did remove the app-side read and send an empty list; Codex round 1 caught why that is unsafe. PostgREST resolves `.rpc()` by argument NAME, so the call still SUCCEEDS against the OLD five-arg function — which short-circuits on `array_length(p_menu_ids, 1) is null` (w23d:190) and voids NOTHING. With the app-side read deleted too, that deployment order captures the full authorization for a sold-out basket, silently. Shipping only the SQL is safe in EVERY order instead: the new function ignores whatever the app sends and derives the set itself; the old function keeps working with the list it is given. **Remove in one later PR, after `supabase db push` has landed:** the `unavailableLines` call in `manual-capture-run.ts`, the `p_menu_ids` argument, and the `gone.length > 0 && voided === 0` cross-check (which exists only because two spellings of the sellability predicate are compared — the SQL parity cases cover that now); then the parameter itself, in a migration that RE-ASSERTS the revoke/grant pair. ⚠️ That migration must not DROP+CREATE without re-granting: a drop resets `pg_proc.proacl` to NULL — EXECUTE **to PUBLIC**, since the revoke belongs to the old `pg_proc` row. Measured: an `authenticated` role could then void lines and mint a `qr_dropped_lines` row with an attacker-chosen `payment_intent`, which `mms_dropped_snapshot` renders back to a diner. `m72_settlement_derives_availability_test.sql` case 9 asserts the privileges. | open        | M72a / Codex #234 round 1                     |
| M72c | med | **The Stripe SDK is constructed with no `timeout` and no `maxNetworkRetries`, so a capture is up to THREE attempts at 80 000 ms each.** `apps/qr/lib/stripe.ts` passes only `apiVersion` and `typescript`; stripe@22.2.1 then applies `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 80000` and `maxNetworkRetries = 2`, retrying on any connection error, on 409, and on every 5xx — i.e. exactly when a capture is slow. This is what makes M72's residual window MINUTES rather than milliseconds, and it is the cheapest lever on that window by a wide margin. Not done inside M72a because it changes retry behaviour for EVERY Stripe call in the app (intents, refunds, Terminal), which deserves its own slice and its own thought about which calls should retry at all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | open        | M72a / measured in node_modules/stripe@22.2.1 |

The right home is `scripts/verify-merge-race.mjs`, which already runs two concurrent sessions in CI and has the mutation harness to prove the guard can fail. Until then this qual is unguarded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | open        | Codex #234 round 2                            |
